newsitem.title: GERMANY: German shares end bourse up but near session lows.
newsitem.headline: German shares end bourse up but near session lows.

text.p: German shares ended bourse trade on Tuesday slightly firmer but off the session peaks as dealers said the market was searching for direction after the recent advance to new all-time record levels.
The 30-share DAX index ended up 10.53 points at 4,381.69 points but well shy of the session peak at 4,398.67 points.
The IBIS DAX, which reflects all-day computer dealings, was down 16.87 points at 4,384.39 points in post-bourse dealings.
A flood of corporate earnings results gave the market fresh fundamentals to digest.

Dresdner Bank AG ended up 2.35 marks at 85.20 marks after saying it planned to raise its base capital by 120 million marks, possibly for "strategic moves", by issuing new shares and was keen to expand its activities in the United States.
The bank, the second-largest in Germany, also said earnings were up 23 percent in the first half of the year.
Commerzbank AG, considered the next target after regional banks Vereinsbank and Hypo-Bank announced plans last week to merge, ended up five pfennigs at 61.75 marks.
Carmaker BMW AG slumped 25 marks to 1,450 marks despite reporting a first-half group net profit of 435 million marks, which was slightly above market expectations for 400 million.
Dealers said other carmakers were benefiting from the positive outlook for the sector, which has been bolstered by the weak mark making exports more competitve.
Daimler-Benz AG, maker of Mercedes vehicles, surged 3.55 marks to 156.45 marks as traders set a near-term target of 160 marks. Daimler will release six-month results on Thursday.

Degussa AG, the metal and chemicals group, was up 3.60 marks at 104.70 marks after reporting a 10 percent rise in nine-month group sales to 11.2 billion marks. Degussa also said it expected a higher profit for the 1996/97 year.

Among other shares posting notable losses in early dealings were sportswear group Puma AG, which was down 2.10 marks at 52.80 marks on more volatile dealings amid fresh takeover talk for the Herzogenaurach-based group.
